title: Unpointed finite Galois torsors descend along affine inverse limits
statement: Let I be a small cofiltered category, D:I→Scheme a diagram of qcqs schemes with affine transition morphisms, and κ:X→D a limiting cone. For every finite group G and finite étale G-torsor Z→X (not necessarily connected), there are an object i, a finite étale G-torsor Z₀→Dᵢ, and a map χ:Z.P→Z₀.P making the square with the projections and κᵢ cartesian. The torsor notion is [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]; qcqs and affine-transition conventions are [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; the square is as in [def-pc-fibre-product].

proof.text: Reindex by a coinitial directed poset using [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex]. The cone remains limiting and qcqs and affine-transition hypotheses persist. A stage of this restriction is an object of I, so a descended cartesian model gives the required model in I.

The finite étale map Z.π is of finite presentation. Descend it by the object clause of [thm-pd-spreading-out], retaining a cartesian comparison. Its stage source is qcqs because it is finitely presented over a qcqs scheme. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite], [lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale], and [lem-weil-pbc-descend-surjective] at a common later stage. Their hypotheses hold: finite presentation gives local finite presentation and local finite type; both stage source and target are qcqs; the limit map has each required property. The result is finite, étale, and surjective.

Enumerate the finite group by a finite type. By the morphism clause of [thm-pd-spreading-out], descend all the action endomorphisms as maps over the base to a common stage. Its equality clause makes the finitely many unit and multiplication equations hold at a later common stage. The comparison map from the finite coproduct of the model to its fibre square is then defined from these action maps.

Finite coproducts and fibre products of finitely presented objects are finitely presented and commute with base change; for coproducts use Mathlib FinitaryPreExtensive.isUniversal_finiteCoproducts in Scheme, and for fibre products use pullback pasting. Consequently the stage comparison pulls back to Z.isIso_sigmaDesc. Descend its inverse and both inverse equations by [thm-pd-spreading-out]. The resulting action and invertible comparison, together with the finite étale surjective map, assemble the required GaloisCover. Pasting the model comparisons gives χ and its cartesian square.

proof_origin.note: The limit-reduction route is unchanged; finite torsor descent is separated from proved section descent and proved base change.

lean.statement:
theorem GaloisCover.exists_stage_of_affine_limits
    {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsCofiltered I] (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    (hDqc : ∀ i, CompactSpace (D.obj i)) (hDqs : ∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i))
    (hDa : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map f))
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (κ : (Functor.const I).obj X ⟶ D)
    (hκ : IsLimit (Cone.mk X κ))
    (G : Type (u + 1)) [Group G] [Finite G] (Z : GaloisCover G X) :
    ∃ (i : I) (Z₀ : GaloisCover G (D.obj i)) (χ : Z.P ⟶ Z₀.P),
      IsPullback χ Z.π Z₀.π (κ.app i)
